prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
Everything is built, published, and rendering correctly through Umbraco's own block grid pipeline.

## What I built

**Content model** (via MCP, in the required order: model → content → templates):
- 4 block element types in `Blocks/`: `heroBlock`, `textBlock`, `imageBlock`, `quoteBlock`
- 2 page types in `Pages/`: `blogFrontPage` (block grid intro) and `blogPost` (date, excerpt, featured image, block grid body) — `blogPost` allowed as a child of `blogFrontPage`, which is now the only allowed child of `siteRoot`
- 2 new Block Grid data types (`Front Page Blocks`, `Blog Post Blocks`), each scoped to the blocks that make sense for that page type
- 6 Unsplash photos imported into a `Blog` media folder

**Content**, all created and published through MCP:
- **Blog** front page (domain `/`) with a hero block + welcome text block, listing both posts by date
- **"Why MCP Is Awesome: Giving AI Real Hands on Your Systems"** — 6 blocks (text/image/text/quote/text/image)
- **"Beyond Chatbots: How MCP Turns Claude into a Teammate Inside Umbraco"** — same structure, different images/copy, and in-world about the very act of building this blog via MCP

**Rendering** (written by hand, per `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiable pipeline — no custom block loops):
- Two templates (`blogFrontPage.cshtml`, `blogPost.cshtml`) calling `Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`
- `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/{heroBlock,textBlock,imageBlock,quoteBlock}.cshtml` adapters mapping ModelsBuilder content to plain models
- `ViewComponents/{Hero,Text,Image,Quote}ViewComponent.cs` + `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml` for the actual markup
- Plain models in `Models/Blocks/`

## How to view it

Umbraco is running at **https://localhost:44317/** (self-signed cert — `-k`/accept-risk in a browser). The two posts are linked from the front page.

## Status / caveats

- One gotcha worth noting for next time: documents created via `create-and-publish-document` **before** a document type has a template end up with `template: null` baked into the content item — assigning `defaultTemplate` afterwards doesn't retroactively fix already-published content. I had to `update-document` (set `template`) + `publish-document` on all three pages after wiring up templates. Doing content creation only after templates exist would avoid this.
- Frontend Tailwind/Vue bundle wasn't built yet in this repo, so I ran `npm install && npm run build` in `Umbraco.Bench.Frontend` to get `wwwroot/dist/site.css` — pages are styled.
- `uSync/` exported everything automatically (document types, data types, templates, content, domains) — not committed since this folder isn't a git repository.
- Everything else checked out clean: no server errors in the log after the template fix, all images load with signed/cropped URLs, and the block grid chrome comes entirely from the shipped `Views/Partials/blockgrid/*` partials — I didn't touch them.
